statement: Use the catalog of Lemma 4.2. On a finite interval of integers h ≥ sR, let Ph be the full partition of R into cells of depth h. On each Q ∈ Ph, let Ph,Q be the orthogonal projection in L2(Q; H) onto constant-coefficient combinations of a subset Mh(Q) ⊂ V(Q). Assume inheritance: if Q′ ∈ Ph+1 is contained in Q, then Mh(Q) ⊂ Mh+1(Q′). Let Ph be the direct sum of the Ph,Q on L2(R; H). Suppose (Fs)s∈S satisfies Equation (4.1). For any integer J ≥ 1 and r1 ≤ t1 ≤ r2 ≤ t2 ≤ · · · ≤ rJ ≤ tJ in the projection depth range and nondecreasing s1, . . . , sJ ∈ S, one has J X j=1 ∥(Ptj − Prj )Fsj ∥2 2 ≤ C2 D|R|. (4.11) If the intervals can be divided into m such ordered families whose reads are nondecreasing, the right side is multiplied by m. For each s ∈ S with s ≥ sR, let Us be any subcollection of the depth-s cells of R. In particular fix an integer ℓ and retain only those s for which s + ℓ and s + ℓ + 1 are in the projection range. Then X s X I∈Us |I| ∥(Ps+ℓ+1 − Ps+ℓ)Fs∥2 2,I ≤ C2 D|R|. (4.12) For every integer L ≥ 0, retaining only s ∈ S with s ≥ sR for which s and s + L are in the projection range,   X s X I∈Us |I| ∥(Ps+L − Ps)Fs∥2 2,I   1/2 ≤ LCD|R|1/2 ≤ (1 + L)CD|R|1/2 .
